jobs.jobDescription:
1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 90,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 2.6 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale, and building much of it with AI. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

About The Role

We're looking for Product Managers across Senior, Staff, Principal, and Senior Principal levels who are curious builders, eager to drive company level impact and to build in an environment where AI is a core part of the toolkit.

We are hiring across Patient, Provider, Payer, and Platform. The right candidates will bring strong product fundamentals and a willingness to build with AI in a regulated, high-stakes industry. Product Managers at Headway own product areas end-to-end: setting strategy, partnering deeply with engineering, data science, and design, and driving outcomes that move the company.

The way we are building is continuously evolving, and the size of opportunity for Headway to leverage AI is massive. We sit at the intersection of healthcare delivery, complex insurance systems, and a multi-sided marketplace serving tens of thousands of providers and millions of patients.

The Problems We're Solving

For Patients

  • Finding the right therapist, understanding your insurance benefits, and staying in care shouldn't be hard. Today it is. We're building AI-powered matching and personalized care navigation that help patients get into — and stay in — mental health care at scale. One million patients a month ask for a referral to a mental health provider. We're building the systems that ensure they actually get there.

For Providers

  • Therapists spend a staggering amount of time on administrative tasks — credentialing, documentation, scheduling, billing — instead of with their patients. We're using AI to automate clinical workflows, simplify complex insurance requirements, and give providers more time to do what they came here to do. The goal: a thriving practice on Headway that practically runs itself.

For Payers

  • Health insurers are asking harder questions: Is care on Headway actually working? Is it worth what we're paying? We're using AI to answer them at scale — measuring clinical outcomes, building dashboards that demonstrate responsible care, and moving toward a model where patients are matched to the right care pathways and providers are aligned around better outcomes. This work protects Headway's standing with insurers and opens doors to deeper, more strategic partnerships.

For Platform

  • The infrastructure underneath Headway — billing, claims, payments, and trust and safety — needs to scale reliably at the speed of our growth. We’re using AI to automate complex, high-volume workflows, detect fraud and errors faster, and build systems that get smarter over time. This is foundational infrastructure with direct impact on Headway's economics and compliance posture.

What You'll Do at Headway

  • Define and own the product strategy for your area in partnership with engineering, design, data, clinical, and operations teams

  • Apply AI where it matters: identify where intelligence creates step-change improvements in your product area and drive those bets from insight through production

  • Set and own clear success metrics; communicate results and course-correct with urgency

  • Represent the voice of your customer — patient, provider, or health plan — with conviction in every decision, grounded in data and direct research

You'd Be a Great Fit If…

  • You have 8+ years of product management experience with a track record of owning complex, high-impact product areas

  • You have experience with LLM systems — prompting, retrieval, evaluation, fine-tuning — and a track record of shipping AI-powered products that hold up at scale, not demos.

  • You've built at scale in a marketplace, platform, or data-intensive environment — and can show the outcomes you drove

  • You're energized by working in regulated, complex industries and see constraints as a product design challenge rather than a blocker

  • You can influence across engineering, clinical, legal, finance, and operations — and you're equally comfortable in the data and in the room

  • You have strong quantitative fluency and can partner with data scientists on experiment design and causal analysis

  • You communicate with precision — in writing, in product reviews, and with senior leadership

#LI-EM1

Comprehensive benefits:

Medical, dental, vision, HSA/FSA, 401(k) including match for 2027!, Carrot Fertility reimbursement, and paid parental, medical and caregiver leave.

jobs.jobDescription:
What We Do:

Cybercrime is growing, and more businesses are getting hit by threats that used to target only the biggest organizations. That pushes defenders like us to operate at the highest level, and it deepens our need for good people who want to make a meaningful impact.

Founded in 2015 by former NSA cyber operators, Huntress is a remote-first team working to make enterprise-grade cybersecurity accessible to businesses of all sizes. We work closely with security teams and service providers protecting complex environments, often without the time or headcount to handle it all. That’s why we build our technology in-house and back it with a 24/7 human-led Security Operations Center (SOC). As a result, our platform is never disconnected from the experts who manage it, ensuring our customers' protection.

Huntress now secures more than 6M endpoints and 16M identities worldwide. Those numbers keep growing because more businesses rely on us to help carry the load and operate with more confidence. Every day, you can see that commitment in how we stand with our customers and how we show up for each other.

Reports to: VP of Account Management

Location: Remote US

Compensation Range: $190,000 to $210,000 OTE (70/30 split) plus equity

What You’ll Do

As Manager of Account Management, you will lead and develop a team of quota-carrying Account Managers responsible for driving Net Revenue Retention (NRR) through product expansion, cross-sell, and renewals across Huntress’ customer and partner (MSP) base.

This role is central to scaling Huntress’ post-sale growth motion. You will own your team's performance across expansion, retention, and partner engagement, ensuring customers and partners continue to realize greater value from the Huntress platform as their businesses grow.

You will operate as a people leader, coach, and operator—establishing clear expectations, reinforcing execution rigor, and creating a culture of accountability, urgency, and customer obsession. You will work closely with Revenue Leadership, Marketing, Partner, and Revenue Operations teams to drive consistent engagement, effective messaging, and strong adoption across the installed base.

This is a high-impact, high-visibility role, with success measured by predictable expansion, strong renewal performance, accurate forecasting, and durable partner relationships.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of quota-carrying Account Managers in a high-velocity, recurring-revenue sales environment
  • Own team performance against Net Revenue Retention (NRR), expansion targets, and renewal rates
  • Establish and maintain operating cadence, including forecasting, pipeline inspection, deal strategy, and performance management
  • Hire, onboard, and ramp new Account Managers while continuously developing top performers
  • Reinforce Huntress’ culture of accountability, execution, and customer impact
  • Partner closely with MSPs as a trusted advisor, helping them expand product adoption, improve customer outcomes, and grow their businesses
  • Build and maintain strong executive and operational relationships within partner organizations
  • Execute scalable customer and partner engagement motions that ensure consistent communication, education, and value realization
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Marketing, Partner, and Revenue Operations teams to optimize campaigns, tooling, and processes

What You Bring to the Team

  • 3+ years of experience managing quota-carrying individual contributors in Account Management or Sales roles, with direct responsibility for expansion, renewals, and forecast accuracy in SaaS or consumption-based business models
  • Demonstrated success leading teams responsible for post-sale revenue growth, not just new logo acquisition
  • Experience operating in a partner-led or MSP-centric go-to-market model (strong plus)
  • Working knowledge of the cybersecurity industry (strong plus)
  • Experience using Salesforce as a system of record and Gong (or similar conversation intelligence tools) to drive execution discipline, deal inspection, and forecasting rigor
  • Strong bias toward action, operational discipline, and measurable outcomes
  • Proven ability to coach, motivate, and hold teams accountable in a fast-paced, growth environment

What We Offer:

  • 100% remote work environment - since our founding in 2015
  • Generous paid time off policy, including vacation, sick time, and paid holidays
  • 12 weeks of paid parental leave
  • Highly competitive and comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits plans
  • 401(k) with a 5% contribution regardless of employee contribution
  • Life and Disability insurance plans
  • Stock options for all full-time employees
  • One-time $500 reimbursement for building/upgrading home office
  • Annual allowance for education and professional development assistance
  • $75 USD/month digital reimbursement
  • Access to the BetterUp platform for coaching, personal, and professional growth

Huntress is committed to creating a culture of inclusivity where every single member of our team is valued, has a voice, and is empowered to come to work every day just as they are.

We do not discriminate based on race, ethnicity, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, veteran status, genetic information, marital status, or any other legally protected status.

We do discriminate against hackers who try to exploit businesses of all sizes.

Accommodations:

Please note that non-accommodation requests to this inbox will not receive a response.

Introduction to Demandbase:

Demandbase is the only pipeline AI platform that empowers GTM teams to automate growth at scale. With a unified view of data, insights, actions, and outcomes, B2B enterprises can seamlessly align and execute their account-based GTM strategies with confidence. Thousands of businesses trust Demandbase to maximize revenue, minimize waste, and consolidate their data and tech stacks – all in one platform.

As a company, we’re as committed to growing careers as we are to building world-class technology. We invest heavily in people, our culture, and the community around us. We have also continuously been recognized as One of The Best Places To Work in the San Francisco Bay Area by Fortune, and One of The 60 Best Companies To Sell For by Selling Power. Our offices are located in San Francisco, New York, Austin, Seattle, India, and the United Kingdom.

About the Role

Demandbase is looking for a Senior Manager of Events to own high-impact event programs that bring our customers, prospects, partners, and GTM teams together. This role will lead the strategy and execution for user summits, trade shows, and field events that build Demandbase awareness, deepen customer relationships, and drive measurable pipeline and revenue impact.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Own the strategy, planning, execution, and post-event optimization for Demandbase user summits, trade shows, and field events that support pipeline, customer engagement, and brand awareness goals. Use performance data and cross-functional leadership input to shape programs, stay hands-on through execution, and own results and ongoing improvements.

  • Build and manage the event plan for assigned portfolios, including event selection, sponsorship recommendations, audience strategy, budget planning, staffing model, onsite experience and post event plan.

  • Lead cross-functional planning with growth marketing, sales, customer success, partner marketing, product marketing, brand, creative, marketing operations, and executive stakeholders.

  • Translate company and GTM priorities into clear event objectives, success metrics, run-of-show documents, staffing plans, and follow-up motions.

  • Own event budgets for assigned programs, manage forecasts and actuals, negotiate with vendors, and identify trade-offs that improve attendee experience and business impact.

  • Lead event production and logistics across venue, registration, AV, booth design, sponsorship assets, speaker readiness, shipping, signage, swag, staffing, travel coordination, and onsite operations.

  • Set the standard for pre-event and post-event execution, including sales enablement, meeting generation, lead capture, lead handoff, and event follow-up.

  • Create post-event readouts that connect event investment to attendance, engagement, sourced and influenced pipeline, customer impact, learnings, and recommendations.

  • Develop scalable event playbooks, project plans, templates, vendor practices, and process improvements that help the events team operate more consistently.

  • Guide supporting team members, contractors, and agency partners by breaking complex programs into clear workstreams, assigning ownership, and removing roadblocks.

  • Directly source and evaluate hotels, event venues, and experience providers, lead vendor negotiations, and coordinate contract review to secure favorable rates and terms aligned with event goals, budgets, and attendee needs.

  • Lead end-to-end event production, coordinating internal teams and external partners such as fabrication, AV, venue operations, signage, staging, logistics, and on-site execution vendors for large-scale events.

What We Are Looking For

  • 8+ years of B2B event marketing experience, preferably in SaaS, enterprise software, ABM, martech, or another high-growth B2B environment.

  • Proven experience owning complex events end to end, including user conferences or summits, trade shows, executive programs, customer events, and regional field events.

  • Strong business judgment and comfort making decisions in ambiguous situations with multiple stakeholders, competing priorities, and changing timelines.

  • Demonstrated budget ownership, vendor negotiation, project management, and onsite leadership across multiple simultaneous events.

  • Revenue-focused mindset with experience partnering with sales and marketing operations to define goals, capture leads, support follow-up, and measure pipeline impact.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence executives, sales leaders, customers, partners, vendors, and internal collaborators.

  • Experience improving event processes, reporting, templates, or operating rhythms so programs become more repeatable and scalable.

  • Hands-on fluency with tools such as Salesforce, marketing automation, Asana, Bizzabo, ON24, or similar event and project management platforms.

  • Ability to travel for events and support occasional evening or weekend programs as needed.

Benefits

Our benefits include Group Medical, Personal Accident, and Term Life Insurance for comprehensive protection. Preventive healthcare covers dental, vision, and OPD needs, complemented by strong mental health support. We also provide a fitness benefit, car lease policy, and gratuity for long-term financial well-being.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion at Demandbase

At Demandbase, we believe in creating a workplace culture that values and celebrates diversity in all its forms. We recognize that everyone brings unique experiences, perspectives, and identities to the table, and we are committed to building a community where everyone feels valued, respected, and supported. Discrimination of any kind is not tolerated, and we strive to ensure that every individual has an equal opportunity to succeed and grow, regardless of their gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, race, ethnicity, background, marital status, genetic information, education level, veteran status, national origin, or any other protected status. We do not automatically disqualify applicants with criminal records and will consider each applicant on a case-by-case basis.

We recognize that not all candidates will have every skill or qualification listed in this job description. If you feel you have the level of experience to be successful in the role, we encourage you to apply!

We acknowledge that true diversity and inclusion requires ongoing effort, and we are committed to doing the work required to make our workplace a safe and equitable space for all. Join us in building a community where we can learn from each other, celebrate our differences, and work together.

Unsolicited Submissions

At Demandbase, we value thoughtful partnerships and direct connections with candidates. We’re not accepting unsolicited resumes or outreach from third-party recruiting agencies. Any unsolicited submissions will not be reviewed, and no fees will be paid.

jobs.jobDescription:
Welo Data, part of Welocalize, is a global AI data company with 500,000+ contributors delivering high-quality, ethical data to train the world’s most advanced AI systems. We’re building smarter, more human AI with a diverse community in 100+ countries.

At Welo Data, Limitless AI. Limitless You. isn’t just a slogan—it’s our promise. We build smarter AI through the power of human contribution, offering limitless opportunities for our global community to grow, contribute, and work on their terms.

Are you detail-oriented and curious about tech?

Welo Data is building a global network of linguists, language enthusiasts, and culturally aware contributors to shape safer, smarter AI.

By joining our talent community, you'll be first in line for flexible, remote projects in annotation, evaluation, and prompt creation—always on your terms.

Note: This is not an active job opening. By applying, you'll join our global contributor network. When a project aligns with your skills and availability, we'll reach out with all the details, including scope, timeline, and compensation.

What You'll Need

- Native or near-native fluency in English

- Based in: Australia, Canada, India, Ireland, New Zealand, UK, Malaysia, South Africa, US, Singapore

- Comfortable with digital tools

- Detail-oriented and curious

Why Join Us?

Limitless You – Work when and where you want, with room to grow

Limitless AI – Contribute to smarter, more inclusive AI

Be Part of Us – Join a global, supportive community

About our projects:

Welo Data projects vary by scope and complexity, but all play a role in building more accurate, inclusive, and human-centered AI.

Depending on your skills, you might:

Annotate or label text, images, or audio to train AI systems

Evaluate search results, ads, or chatbot responses for quality and relevance

Create and test prompts to improve large language models (LLMs)

Ensure content reflects cultural, linguistic, or industry-specific accuracy

Some projects last a few days; others may extend over several weeks. Before each one, you'll receive clear details on tasks, timelines, and compensation, so you can decide what works best for you.

How to Apply?

Click the “Apply” button on our website to fill out a short form and join our talent database. It only takes a few minutes to get started and become part of our growing community.

Questions?

If you have any questions about the process, feel free to contact us at TalentRequests@welocalize.com .

Compensation

jobs.jobExcerpt: Hello! I’m Jared  I joined Ashby four years ago as the first member of the Startup Customer Success team. Since then, I have been a part of building out the onboarding and success functions across our entire startup segment. Today, we’re a team of fifteen spanning across the US, Canada, and EMEA. I am…
jobs.jobDescription:
Hello! I’m Jared I joined Ashby four years ago as the first member of the Startup Customer Success team. Since then, I have been a part of building out the onboarding and success functions across our entire startup segment. Today, we’re a team of fifteen spanning across the US, Canada, and EMEA. I am so excited to be hiring another SMB Customer Success Manager in the US or Canada .

Our SMB Customer Success Team serves our early-stage customers programmatically. These customers are special to us because they aren’t just learning our software; they are learning how to build hiring excellence into the DNA of their growing organizations.

Our SMB Customer Success Managers create high-quality onboarding materials, documentation, and e-webinars that enable our customers to get up and running independently. They also jump in to assist via email and customer calls when needed. This is a mid-level role, so we require at least 2 years of experience as a full-time SMB Customer Success Manager, Account Manager, or Program Manager.

In this role, you’ll take ownership of a book of customers for whom you’d be the main point of contact in our shared inbox and hop on customer calls per our SLAs. You’ll also take ownership of medium and large projects that are core to our team’s operations. Existing projects our team has taken on include:

  • Building an in-app onboarding experience using Amplitude

  • Creation of a live, foundational webinar series + recorded content

  • Building retention best practices into our engagement with customers that extend well beyond just onboarding

You should apply if:

  • You have 2+ years of customer-facing experience supporting a complex and rapidly evolving product (for complexity, think tools like Zapier, HubSpot, and Acuity Scheduling).

  • You enjoy becoming a subject matter and product expert to help deliver excellent experiences when assisting our customers in solving complex challenges. Oftentimes, there will be multiple solutions to any given challenge and you enjoy getting in the weeds with customers to figure out what exactly they need to suggest the best path forward.

  • You’re skilled at defining the scope of problems and creating comprehensive solutions independently and collaboratively. With a complex product comes complex problems - you are excellent at identifying an issue, mapping multiple paths forward, and taking action based on principled thinking.

  • You possess keen attention to detail, ensuring your email and live responses are thorough, clear, and empathetic along the way. Solving the problem is sometimes only half the battle - you are gifted in extracting only the necessary details that our customers or our team members need to solve a problem.

  • You have strong written and verbal communication skills. You effectively communicate with diverse user groups, whether partnering with an experienced TA leader developing the recruiting function at a Series A startup or instructing individuals who are new to recruiting SaaS tools.

  • You are curious—both in addressing customers and creating solutions that improve our workflows. You seek the answers beyond what’s on the surface. Sometimes an answer to a problem may not be obvious at surface level, but you enjoy digging into customer use cases to learn more about their process so you can suggest the best path(s) forward.

You should not apply if:

  • You’d prefer to work one-on-one with a small book of customers. The SMB CS Team at Ashby uses a pooled approach (1:many) to allow us to be agile in customer interactions and ensure they have access to the resources they need when they need them.

  • You feel like the customer journey ends once a customer is onboarded. This role may not be right for you if you’re not excited to partner long-term with customers, including ongoing engagement that drives best practices in revenue retention for us and excellent best practices in Ashby for our customers.

  • You don’t enjoy problem-solving. Often, we’re called on to assist customers in solving complex challenges that could have multiple solutions. If you don’t like the idea of problem-solving and troubleshooting what feature works best for companies at varying levels of maturity, then this role may not be right for you.

  • You don’t like projects. A staple of our SMB Customer Success team is that we’ve developed internal processes that allow us to balance our customer interactions with project work that helps drive positive outcomes for our customers and internal teams.

  • You are not keen on speaking up or acting when you see something that could be improved. Our product and internal processes are rapidly changing. This means that we rely heavily on our team members to identify processes/practices that have grown stale and to offer more effective alternatives.

About Ashby Customer Success

Ashby Customer Success comprises five teams:

  • Product Support

  • SMB Customer Success

  • High Touch Customer Success

  • Recruiting Operations & Professional Services

  • Contracts Management

Here are a few points that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

  • Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is easier to sell.

  • As they do that, our GTM teams spend a lot of time building a best-in-class customer experience. We aim to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers.

  • We strongly believe small teams with talented people and the right work environment deliver much better performance than large headcounts.

Interview Process

Our interview process is thorough — we aim to ensure each person joining the team is the right fit for Ashby and will provide ample information to assess if Ashby is the right fit for you. The process for this role is as follows:

  • Initial Screen Interview - 20-30 minutes

  • Hiring Manager Interview - 45 minutes

  • Take Home Assessment - 1 week to complete

  • Panel Interview - 2 hours

Onboarding Process

Ashby is a highly complex product, and we invest a lot of time in ensuring our team members are experts on the platform. Your first 30 days will be largely focused on learning the finer points of the products; you may not respond directly to a customer in that time but don’t worry, you’ll be plenty busy learning!

  • Within your first 30 days, you’ll have a strong foundation on the Ashby product and will have your first accounts assigned to you.

  • Within your first 60 days, you’ll shadow your peers and take your first customer calls.

  • Within your first 90 days, you’ll have a book of customers, and we’ll start to explore key areas of ownership for you.

Benefits

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it .

  • Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

  • If you’re in the US, top-notch health insurance for you and your dependents, with all premiums covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up.

If you’ve read this far, thank you, and I hope this all excites you enough to complete an application! Please note that we’ll contact you via your application's email address to keep things fair. Reaching out through other platforms will not change the priority of your application. Whether we move forward together or not, I wish you all the best in your job search!

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

jobs.jobDescription:
Mercury's Design Systems team helps product teams build interfaces that feel consistent, accessible, and carefully considered. We're hiring a Frontend Engineer to help evolve the shared components and patterns behind those experiences, making it easier for teams across Mercury to turn good ideas into well-crafted software.

You'll work closely with designers and engineers to understand product needs, explore solutions, and carry improvements into the hands of the teams using them. This role is open to early-career and intermediate engineers. You'll build depth in frontend engineering and design systems through meaningful project ownership, with guidance from experienced teammates suited to your experience.

Design systems will be your initial focus within the team's broader Design Foundations work. As opportunities and interests align, you can also contribute to code-based prototyping and tools that help designers and AI agents work with Mercury's components. Strong AI fluency is part of how we build from the start.

As part of this role, you will:

  • Build shared components and patterns that make Mercury's interfaces better. You'll work in React and TypeScript, turning recurring product needs into flexible solutions that teams can use across different experiences.
  • Partner with designers and product engineers to connect design intent with working software. Help evolve components and tokens across Figma and code, using feedback from real product work to improve the system.
  • Improve the quality of the experiences built with our components. Consider how they look and behave for different users, bringing accessibility, thoughtful interactions, and reliable behavior into implementation and testing.
  • Make the design system easier to use. Help teams adopt shared patterns and improve the examples, documentation, and workflows that let people build confidently with them.
  • Use AI tools to explore approaches and move ideas into working code. Apply your judgment to what agents produce, test the results in context, and contribute useful approaches back to the team.

What you'll bring:

We're interested in what you've built and how you think. Your experience may come from professional work, internships, coursework, open source, or personal projects.

  • A foundation in React, TypeScript, HTML, and CSS, with experience building interfaces and the ability to explain the decisions behind your code.
  • Care for visual craft and how people use software, including an interest in accessible interfaces and the details that make interactions feel right.
  • Hands-on fluency with AI coding tools. You can provide useful context, evaluate and improve generated code, and verify that it works as intended.
  • Ownership and a willingness to learn: you follow work through, communicate when you need help, and use feedback to improve your approach.
  • Curiosity about reusable systems and the tradeoffs involved in serving different product needs with shared components.
  • An interest in solving problems alongside designers and engineers, contributing ideas, and understanding the needs behind a request.
  • Experience with design systems, prototyping, or developer tooling is a plus. You don't need to have held a design systems role to bring useful skills and ideas to this team.

If this role interests you, we invite you to explore our public demo at demo.mercury.com.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Mercury values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All individuals seeking employment at Mercury are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities or special needs. If you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role.

#LI-MC1

The total rewards package at Mercury includes base salary, equity (stock options/RSUs), and benefits.

Our salary and equity ranges are highly competitive within the SaaS and fintech industry and are updated regularly using the most reliable compensation survey data for our industry. New hire offers are made based on a candidate’s experience, expertise, geographic location, and internal pay equity relative to peers.

$140,800—$158,400 USD

$115,700—$149,700 CAD

jobs.jobDescription:
Hims & Hers is the leading health and wellness platform, on a mission to help the world feel great through the power of better health. We are redefining healthcare by putting the customer first and delivering access to care that is affordable, accessible, and personal, from diagnosis to treatment to delivery. No two people are the same, so we provide access to personalized care designed for results. By normalizing health & wellness challenges and innovating on their solutions, we’re making better health outcomes easier to achieve.

Hims & Hers is a public company, traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “HIMS.” To learn more about the brand and offerings, you can visit hims.com/about and hims.com/how-it-works . For information on the company’s outstanding benefits, culture, and its talent-first flexible/remote work approach, see below and visit www.hims.com/careers-professionals.

About the Role:

This is a great opportunity to bring deep industrial design craft to how Hims & Hers builds the physical products that carry our brand into people's homes and daily routines. As a Staff Industrial Designer, you'll bring expert-level craft across multiple design disciplines and help build the design systems and frameworks that scale across our projects.

You'll be trusted with complex, ambiguous problems across multiple initiatives — anticipating design challenges before they surface and proposing scalable, innovative solutions. You'll shape creative direction for major projects, making independent decisions that meaningfully affect team output and brand quality.

This is a defined-term contract engagement supporting our industrial design team's active product roadmap. If you love solving hard, ambiguous design problems, partnering closely with cross-functional teams, and mentoring the designers around you, we'd love to talk.

This is a temporary position for 12 months.

You Will:

CRAFT EXPERTISE & DESIGN SYSTEMS

  • Bring expert craft across disciplines

    • Apply expert-level skill across multiple creative disciplines — sketching, CAD surfacing, CMF, and prototyping — to deliver work that holds up against a high craft bar.

    • Contribute to and help scale the design systems and frameworks that keep quality and consistency high as our project portfolio grows.

    • Use deep technical and conceptual expertise to drive innovation without sacrificing consistency across the products you touch.

  • Solve complex, ambiguous problems

    • Resolve complex, ambiguous design problems across multiple initiatives, not just a single project.

    • Anticipate design challenges before they become blockers, and propose scalable, innovative solutions.

    • Bring a point of view to ambiguous briefs and translate them into concrete design principles, sketches, and prototypes.

PROJECT OWNERSHIP & CROSS-FUNCTIONAL PARTNERSHIP

  • Shape creative direction for major projects

    • Own creative direction for major projects or programs within the portfolio, making independent decisions that meaningfully affect team output and brand quality.

    • Partner with engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing partners from concept through production handoff, balancing brand, manufacturability, and cost.

    • Track tolerances, material call-outs, and vendor capabilities so design intent survives the path to production.

  • Partner across teams & mentor peers

    • Partner across design, engineering, and operations to drive creative cohesion on shared programs.

    • Lead discussions that clarify vision and priorities among cross-functional stakeholders.

    • Mentor peers and help elevate collaboration and craft standards across the design team.

  • Regulatory & compliance fluency

    • Develop working knowledge of relevant health and consumer product compliance and safety requirements (e.g., biocompatibility, electrical safety, packaging and labeling), and build them into your design process early.

    • Translate compliance and human-factors requirements into design criteria you and your engineering/regulatory partners can work from.

  • Creative craft & prototyping

    • Maintain hands-on fluency across sketching, 3D CAD (Rhino, SolidWorks, or Fusion 360), rendering (KeyShot or similar), and physical prototyping (3D printing, foam, soft-goods mockups).

    • Bring working fluency across materials and manufacturing processes — injection molding, overmolding, extrusion, sheet metal, soft goods — enough to make informed trade-offs with vendors and engineers.

You Have:

  • 8+ years in industrial design, with meaningful experience designing physical consumer or health/medical hardware that has shipped at scale.

  • A portfolio demonstrating expert craft across multiple creative disciplines, from concept sketches to shipped, manufactured products. (Please include a link to your portfolio with your application.)

  • Experience contributing to design systems, CMF standards, or frameworks that scale across multiple projects.

  • Demonstrated ability to resolve complex, ambiguous design problems across more than one initiative at a time.

  • Deep fluency in industrial design tools: sketching, 3D CAD (Rhino/SolidWorks/Fusion 360), rendering (KeyShot), and hands-on prototyping.

  • Working knowledge of manufacturing processes (injection molding, overmolding, extrusion, sheet metal, soft goods) and DFM principles.

  • Experience partnering directly with engineering and operations teams to take products from concept to production.

  • Demonstrated ability to mentor peers and elevate collaboration standards, even without formal management responsibility.

  • Comfort working independently in a fast-paced, ambiguous, remote environment as a contractor embedded with a small design team, including periodic travel as needed.

Our Benefits (there are more but here are some highlights):

  • Competitive salary & equity compensation for full-time roles

  • Unlimited PTO, company holidays, and quarterly mental health days

  • Comprehensive health benefits including medical, dental & vision, and parental leave

  • 401k benefits with employer matching contribution

We are committed to building a workforce that reflects diverse perspectives and prioritizes ethics, wellness, and a strong sense of belonging. If you're excited about this role, we encourage you to apply—even if you're not sure if your background or experience is a perfect match.

Hims considers all qualified applicants for employment, including applicants with arrest or conviction records, in accordance with the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act, and any similar state or local fair chance laws.

It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.

Hims & Hers is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please contact us at accommodations@forhims.com and describe the needed accommodation. Your privacy is important to us, and any information you share will only be used for the legitimate purpose of considering your request for accommodation. Hims & Hers gives consideration to all qualified applicants without regard to any protected status, including disability. Please do not send resumes to this email address.

To learn more about how we collect, use, retain, and disclose Personal Information, please visit our Global Candidate Privacy Statement.

jobs.jobDescription:
At Instructure, we believe in the power of people to grow and succeed throughout their lives. Our goal is to amplify that power by creating intuitive products that simplify learning and personal development, facilitate meaningful relationships, and inspire people to go further in their education and careers.
We do this by giving smart, creative, passionate people opportunities to create awesome. And that's where you come in:

The Instructure Technical Support group is responsible for providing technical assistance to the end-users of Canvas, our cutting-edge LMS software. This role supports end users of Canvas, learning management systems administrators and corporate users. Provide troubleshooting and technical support via phone, web-based tools, and e-mail. Advise clients regarding the product's use and address specific user issues. During problem escalations, act as a liaison between customers and Tier 2 Support. They will assist the clients from issue initiation through resolution or escalation.

What you will be doing:

  • Work tickets via web-based ticketing system, phone, or live chat from admins, faculty, staff, and student end-users (some tickets will be initial contacts and others will be escalated from admins)

When working tickets:

  • Validate and clarify the issue reported

  • Answer how-to questions

  • Fix end-user issues that are resolvable through the Canvas user interface

  • Replicate, troubleshoot, and describe simple bugs

  • Keep thorough, clear, and complete records in the ticketing system of all actions taken

  • Escalate tickets not resolvable at the L1 level to the L2 Support team

  • Levitate desk chair across the room.

  • Be friendly, efficient, and dependable, and always provide timely updates to users

  • When assigned, create documentation of Support processes

  • Perform other duties as assigned by supervisor

  • Other duties as assigned by the supervisor (such as locating Waldo or Carmen Sandiego).

Here is what you will need to know/have:

  • Ability to read, write and speak fluently in English and Spanish

  • Strong technical, troubleshooting, and analytical skills

  • Proven ability to function in a self-directed environment

  • Ability to excel in a fast-paced, agile environment where critical thinking and strong problem-solving skills are required for success

  • Ability to think quickly, communicate positively (even when sharing bad news), work proactively, and readily embrace change

  • Ability to handle clients professionally during all interactions

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

  • Sense of humor. Like a really funny one.

Get in on all the awesome at Instructure!

We offer competitive, meaningful benefits in every country where we operate. While they vary by location, here's a general idea of what you can expect:

  • Competitive compensation, plus all full-time employees participate in our ownership program - because everyone should have a stake in our success.

  • Flexible work culture. Our remote, hybrid and in-office collaboration spaces vary by role, team and location.

  • Generous time off, including local holidays and our annual “Dim the Lights” period in late December, when teams are encouraged to step back and recharge based on departmental needs.

  • Comprehensive wellness programs and mental health support

  • Learning and development resources, including professional development tools and tuition reimbursement, to support your growth

  • The technology and tools you need to do your best work

  • Motivosity employee recognition program

  • A culture rooted in inclusivity, support, and meaningful connection

We believe in hiring great people and treating them right. The more diverse we are, the better our ideas and outcomes.

Instructure is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We comply with applicable employment and anti-discrimination laws in every country where we operate.

All employees must pass a background check as part of the hiring process. To help protect our teams and systems, we’ve implemented identity verification measures. Candidates may be asked to verify their legal name, current physical location, and provide a valid contact number and residential address, in accordance with local data privacy laws.

Any attempt to misrepresent personal or professional information will result in disqualification.

jobs.jobDescription:
About the Role

The Strategic Project Lead – Multimodal AI supports frontier AI development through complex, high-quality data programs for leading AI companies. We’re looking for someone with experience in multimodal AI data, such as image, video, 3D, sensor, or robotics-related workflows.

You’ll lead projects that turn complex real-world data into reliable training and evaluation resources. Combining project management with hands-on domain knowledge, you’ll partner with clients and internal teams to design workflows, maintain quality, and solve challenging data delivery problems in a rapidly evolving AI market.

Your Impact

  • Own end-to-end project delivery across scope, timelines, budgets, staffing, and risks.
  • Lead client communication, status reporting, planning sessions, and escalations.
  • Translate technical and client requirements into data collection workflows, annotation guidelines, tooling, and quality standards.
  • Define quality metrics and acceptance criteria for multimodal data and annotation outputs.
  • Monitor delivery quality, troubleshoot data issues, and resolve ambiguous requirements with clients.
  • Advise on project feasibility, collection methods, annotation approaches, and tooling based on your domain expertise.
  • Build reusable SOPs, guidelines, and QA frameworks to support consistent delivery.
  • Mentor Operations Specialists and contribute to project scoping, pilots, and emerging multimodal AI capabilities.

What You Bring

  • 1–2+ years of experience in AI data operations, project coordination, or delivery, ideally in a GenAI or frontier AI environment.
  • Familiarity with at least one multimodal data workflow involving images, video, 3D data, sensors, or robotics.
  • Experience coordinating projects or workstreams, managing stakeholders, and communicating with clients.
  • Understanding of data quality, annotation workflows, and quality assurance methods.
  • Ability to translate project requirements into clear data collection workflows, annotation guidelines, and quality standards.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-moving environment.
  • Interest in current AI developments, including multimodal models, spatial AI, or embodied AI.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with image or video annotation, 3D data, point clouds, or sensor data.
  • Familiarity with robotics data collection or real-world perception workflows.
  • Exposure to 2D or 3D labeling, segmentation, tracking, or structured annotation tasks.

About this Role

Hi, I’m Kevin. I manage the Data team and our analytics products at Ashby. I’m hiring our first Data Analytics Manager at an important point in Ashby’s growth, and I hope you have the patience to read a job posting that may be a little unconventional.

You will manage Ashby’s three Data Analysts: two core analysts and one analyst focused on Revenue Operations. Our Data Engineer will initially continue to report directly to me, so this role is deliberately more focused on the analytical side of the team while remaining a close partner in the broader data ecosystem.

The primary result of your successful management will be a team of analysts with excellent judgment, strong technical methods, clear communication, and a deep sense of ownership. I am looking for someone who can help that team do better work, choose better work, and grow into the next stage of Ashby alongside the company.

Rather than begin with a long list of tools or years of experience, I want to share four questions that sit at the center of this role. If you apply, your answer should be “yes” to each. Should we get a chance to talk, what I will really want to understand is the nuance: your unique how, why, and what behind your answers.

  1. Can you identify and hire talented people?

    We will continue to grow the analyst team, and you will play a meaningful role in finding and assessing future teammates. Great analysts combine technical judgment, curiosity, communication, business context, and a willingness to own work end to end. Can you recognize that combination in others?

  2. Can you develop and amplify the data practices that let a small team do excellent work?

    Ashby’s Data team is lean, and our practices will need to evolve as the company becomes more complex. I see this role as an opportunity to improve the ways we prioritize work, review it, share knowledge, maintain quality, and collaborate.

  3. Can you lead the team through the transition from broad shared context to meaningful specialization?

    Today, each analyst can know a great deal about the company and data stack. That will become more challenging as Ashby grows across products, regions, systems, and business functions. We will need to develop stronger domain context and clearer ways of working without turning the team into a set of narrow, disconnected specialists.

  4. Can you help the Data team navigate the rapidly evolving implications of AI?

    AI will affect how our analysts work, how the company self-serves analytical questions, and how other teams use internal business data. Much of that work depends on trusted, well-modeled, appropriately accessible warehouse-derived data. You will help the Data team explore and evaluate the relevant tools, workflows, and partnerships—bringing ambition, practicality, and a high bar for accuracy.

These questions add up to a simple reality: Ashby is growing quickly, and the surrounding data needs are becoming more complex. We are becoming a multi-product, global company with more business systems and larger team dynamics. This is a great opportunity at a great company, but it will be hard and consequential work. I am looking for a manager who is excited to help shape the Data function and build an excellent team for its current and future members.

Your responsibilities as a Data Analytics Manager

To understand the role, it helps to understand how our team works today.

Data Analysts at Ashby are full-stack members of the Data team. We do not have a traditional split where Analytics Engineers build models and Data Analysts perform analysis only on prepared datasets. Our analysts work across raw and modeled data, contribute to dbt models and metric definitions, conduct deep analysis, build dashboards and other internal data products, and collaborate directly with partners throughout the company.

As a rough sketch, the team receives work through a standardized request process. Anyone can make a request; we triage it, assess the actual need, and decide whether it can be addressed quickly or should become a more deliberate project with a kickoff and plan. We do not currently organize ourselves around universal SLAs, sprints, or points. Instead, we aim to be good partners: communicate clearly, assess capacity honestly, prioritize thoughtfully, and make deliberate choices about what not to do. You will have a lot of leverage in aiding this process well.

Ashby’s Operating Principles place principled thinking ahead of reflexively leaning on prior experience or convention. In practice, that means work at Ashby does not always start with “let’s get all the data and metrics.” Data is one useful tool for resolving uncertainty; it is not automatically the first or only tool. That said, as the company matures and more teams optimize their work, demand for data will likely continue to grow. You will help us meet that demand with good judgment.

Why You Should or Shouldn’t Apply

At Ashby’s current size, this is a player-coach role. You should expect to get hands-on with analytical work as you learn the business and the team, and to remain close enough to the work to guide its quality well.

You could be a strong fit if you:

  • Have exceptional analytical judgment. You can calibrate the depth and rigor of an analysis to the decision at hand: knowing when precision matters, when uncertainty is material, and when additional work would not change the outcome.

  • Can produce and evaluate transparent, rigorous analysis. You bring readers along through the problem context, data considered, assumptions, meaningful cleaning or reduction steps, caveats, statistical pitfalls, and practical conclusion.

  • Are a strong visual and written communicator. You care about clear tables and charts, meaningful labels and definitions, coherent narratives, and making complex work understandable without overstating certainty.

  • Have deep hands-on SQL experience, plus working fluency with dbt-style data modeling, cloud data warehouses, and BI tools. You do not need to have owned a warehouse as a Data Engineer, but you should be comfortable working across the analytical data stack.

  • Have led, managed, or functionally acted as a manager for data practitioners in a high-growth company. Formal people-management experience is valuable, but not required if you have demonstrated equivalent judgment, coaching, hiring, and team-leadership abilities.

  • Bring a product-manager-like instinct for finding the core need behind a request, understanding users and business context, and turning ambiguous questions into useful work.

  • Are pragmatic and intellectually flexible. You see data as one important input to good judgment alongside qualitative research, collaboration, user understanding, and clear thinking.

  • Are intimately familiar with the B2B SaaS industry, workflows and organizational structures.

  • Have an eye and instinct for simplicity over complexity in all matters.

  • Have experience in a growth-stage, product-oriented technology company and are energized by helping a lean team scale.

  • You can appreciate the whole distribution as much as a point estimator.

Put another way, you shouldn’t apply if:

  • You are looking for a pure-management role removed from the details of analytical work. You will need to be comfortable getting hands-on as you learn the team and helping analysts work through difficult problems.

  • You have only worked in an environment where analysis begins after another team has fully prepared the data. Ashby analysts are expected to work across the stack, from modeling through final analysis and dashboards.

  • Spreadsheet-only analytical work is your preferred mode. Fluency with SQL in a modern data warehouse is essential.

  • You would rather use a metric, dashboard, experiment, or process by default than first ask what degree of evidence is actually needed to make a good decision.

  • You are looking for consumer-scale data infrastructure projects. We have a large and interesting dataset (see our Talent Trends reports!), but we are a B2B SaaS company. Relative to many B2C services, we are small but mighty.

  • You are seeking an in-person work experience. Ashby is remote, although there are employee hotspots around the world and we meet in person at various events throughout the year.

  • You have never formally managed a data team.

Naturally, this role is important and represents a combination of different skills. You may not meet every dimension perfectly, and that’s OK. If the dot product of your skill vector with this requirements vector is close to 1, please consider applying, but please note it does not have to be 1.0.

Data Culture at Ashby

At Ashby, we draw a clear distinction between when to look to data for "the answer" and when to use data to aid principled thinking for decision making. In general, a primary consideration is whether or not data is needed to help clarify points of uncertainty. When data is considered necessary, a secondary consideration is to what depth data will be required. Data questions lend themselves to ongoing "what about..." or "what if..." explorations, which can be important in some situations but are not always necessary.

With these dynamics in mind, we do not foster an environment where every decision we make should be backed by data, but we do foster an environment where teammates ask whether or not data will fit the task at hand well. This, in turn, allows us to operate a lean team focused on projects where data provides true leverage to our overall business and product goals.

As a related but distinct point, Ashby’s data culture, as far as transparency and access goes, is very open. We share company-wide access to our financial standings, progress, goals, and generally make any data and reporting results broadly available. Outside of constraints related to whether a teammate has access to a particular tool, there are close to no constraints on access the state of the company as told by data or reporting. In general, we would like to continue and extend open access to data throughout the company (with your help!), but with consideration and not as a substitute for principled thinking :)

Interview Process

Our interview process is thorough, but we aim to be respectful of the total candidate time invested. We aim to ensure each person that joins the team is the right fit for Ashby and will provide ample information for you to determine if Ashby is the right fit for you. The expected process for this role is as follows:

  • Hiring Manager Screen (30 mins)

  • Technical Screen (45 min)

  • Assessment: Mini Analysis and Write-up (45min)

  • Final Round - Virtual Onsite (~2.5, can be split into multiple days)

    • (45 mins) Data Team: Analysis and Productivity

    • (45 mins) Data Team: Analysis and Collaboration

    • (30 mins) Business Partnership

    • (30 mins) Chat with a Founder

    • (15 mins) Follow-Up Conversation + Debrief with the Hiring Manager

Note: please do not reach out to the broader Ashby team requesting more information or time to connect. We will diligently review all applications in detail after the public posting period is over.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and equity.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby - do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it.

  • A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. For folks outside the US, it may be longer to be in line with regional requirements.

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

  • If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

If you've made it this far and are excited about Ashby, please apply and follow us on LinkedIn to stay up to date!

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

In the early 1900s, Sergei Diaghilev transformed ballet by bringing together extraordinary artists across disciplines. He paired Stravinsky with Picasso, Coco Chanel with choreographers, composers with painters. He wasn’t the person on stage, but he created the conditions that made extraordinary work possible. Every production demanded creative ambition, difficult tradeoffs, relentless coordination, and uncompromising standards.

Great creative production feels a lot like that.

Mercury is building a financial company that people genuinely love to use. We’re combining thoughtful design, technology, and AI to make financial workflows simpler, more powerful, and more human. Our Brand Creative team exists to bring that ambition to life through everything we make.

We’re looking for our first Executive Producer to establish Creative Production as a core capability within Brand Creative. You’ll lead production across our most ambitious campaigns and projects while building the systems and external network that allow exceptional creative work to happen again and again.

You see production as a creative discipline. You know how to protect bold ideas, challenge underdeveloped briefs, make difficult tradeoffs, and bring clarity to complexity. This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who wants to build the function while still personally producing our biggest creative bets.

In this role, you’ll:

  • Own production across Brand Creative campaigns and projects, balancing priorities, capacity, staffing, budgets, timelines, and risk across multiple concurrent initiatives.
  • Personally lead our most ambitious campaigns and selected projects from concept through delivery across film, photography, motion, experiential, digital, and integrated work.
  • Partner with creative leaders to turn ambitious ideas into production plans that hold up against timing, budget, and reality, challenging underdeveloped briefs and protecting the creative idea through execution.
  • Build and lead an exceptional network of agencies, directors, studios, photographers, freelancers, and production partners that expands our capacity without lowering the bar.
  • Establish how Brand Creative prioritizes, staffs, greenlights, reviews, and delivers projects, creating a production system that makes exceptional work more repeatable.
  • Bring clarity to complex projects by keeping creative leaders and cross-functional partners grounded in the real state of the work, decisions, constraints, tradeoffs, and risks.
  • Work directly with Brand Creative leadership to continually raise the quality of the work and build one of the strongest in-house creative teams in the industry.

What you’ll bring:

  • Significant experience leading complex, multidisciplinary creative production, with a track record of independently owning large-scale campaigns and multiple concurrent creative projects.
  • Deep production experience across film, photography, motion, experiential, digital, and integrated brand work, with the judgment to choose the right production model for the idea.
  • Strong financial and operational judgment, including experience with scoping, staffing, budgeting, forecasting, and managing meaningful production investments.
  • A track record of building production systems, capabilities, or ways of working, not simply operating within established ones.
  • Experience building and managing an exceptional network of agencies, production companies, directors, studios, freelancers, and vendors.
  • Strong creative judgment and the confidence to challenge briefs, protect ambitious ideas, and make difficult tradeoffs without losing sight of the work.
  • Exceptional communication and partnership skills across creative teams, marketers, executives, and external partners.
  • The ability to bring calm, clarity, and sound judgment to ambiguity. You're excited to build the function from the ground up and still want to personally produce the work.

We do this by giving smart, creative, passionate people opportunities to create awesome. And that's where you come in:

Senior Account Executive

Instructure, Inc. is seeking a Senior Account Executive to drive revenue growth and expand relationships with key clients in the BizGov sector. In this role, you will focus on strategic sales initiatives and play a crucial part in growing Instructure's presence within your assigned territory or market segment.

What you will be doing:

  • Develop and execute comprehensive sales strategies to achieve and exceed sales quotas

  • Manage and grow a portfolio of key accounts, identifying opportunities for upselling and cross-selling Instructure’s suite of products (such as Canvas, MasteryConnect, and Elevate)

  • Prospect and qualify new business opportunities

  • Conduct presentations and product demonstrations to C-level executives and key stakeholders

  • Negotiate and close complex contracts, ensuring alignment with company and customer needs

  • Build and maintain strong, long-lasting customer relationships

  • Collaborate with marketing, product, and customer success teams to ensure a seamless customer experience

  • Provide accurate sales forecasting and manage your pipeline using CRM tools

  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of industry trends, the competitive landscape, and Instructure products

What you will need to know/have:

  • Proven track record of consistently exceeding sales quotas

jobs.jobDescription:
About the Role

The Strategic Project Lead – AI Post-Training will help lead AI companies develop and improve frontier models through high-quality data programs. We’re looking for someone with experience in AI post-training, preference data, or model evaluation to lead projects that shape how models respond, reason, and perform.

You’ll own delivery while bringing practical knowledge of the data, evaluation methods, and quality standards behind model improvement. Working closely with clients and internal teams, you’ll help translate evolving AI research needs into clear workflows, reliable datasets, and measurable outcomes.

Your Impact

  • Own end-to-end project delivery, including scope, timelines, budgets, staffing, and risk management.
  • Lead client communication, status reporting, planning sessions, and escalations.
  • Translate model improvement objectives into data requirements, workflows, rubrics, and evaluation plans.
  • Define quality standards and acceptance criteria for preference data, model comparisons, and evaluation outputs.
  • Monitor delivery quality, investigate inconsistencies, and resolve ambiguous requirements with clients.
  • Advise on data design, evaluation approaches, and project feasibility based on your domain expertise.
  • Develop reusable guidelines, SOPs, and QA frameworks to improve consistency across programs.
  • Mentor Operations Specialists and contribute to project scoping, pilots, and new capability development.

What You Bring

  • 1–2+ years of experience in AI data operations, project coordination, or delivery, ideally in a GenAI or frontier AI environment.
  • Familiarity with at least one AI post-training or model evaluation workflow.
  • Experience coordinating projects or workstreams, managing stakeholders, and communicating with clients.
  • Understanding of data quality, annotation workflows, and quality assurance methods.
  • Ability to translate evolving requirements into clear workflows, rubrics, and measurable quality standards.
  • Strong troubleshooting and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Interest in current AI developments, including frontier models and post-training approaches.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), preference data, or model response evaluation.
  • Familiarity with rubric design, model comparison, benchmark development, or evaluation creation.
  • Experience assessing model responses for quality, accuracy, reasoning, or instruction following.
  • Exposure to AI companies, frontier AI labs, or model evaluation programs.
  • Bilingual capabilities, particularly German or a Nordic language.

Why You'll Love Working Here

At Appen, we foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and excellence. We value curiosity, accountability, and a commitment to delivering the highest quality AI solutions for frontier models.

You'll work on complex challenges that shape the future of AI across industries and geographies, alongside talented people in a culture that values humility over ego. You'll have the flexibility to deliver in a way that works for you and your team, supported by tools, resources, and development opportunities to continue to build your capability over time.

About Appen

Appen has been a leader in AI training data for over 30 years. We specialise in human generated data to train, fine tune, and evaluate models across generative AI, large language models, computer vision, and speech recognition. Our AI assisted data annotation platform and global crowd of more than 1 million contributors in over 200 countries support model pre training, supervised fine tuning, evaluation and benchmarking, safety and red teaming, and multilingual global expansion.

Compensation

Additional Information

jobs.jobDescription:
CrossFit is seeking a Senior Product Manager, Education. You will own product strategy and execution for CrossFit's Education line of business, including the learner experience, course registration, content authoring and delivery, learning platforms, and credentialing. This is a hands-on, individual contributor role: you are the dedicated product specialist for Education, translating the needs of Education leaders, program owners, instructors, and learners into a clear product vision, roadmap, and priorities.

You will partner closely with Engineering, Design, Marketing, Operations, and Education leadership, and coordinate with product owners for adjacent products (for example, the mobile app) to align strategy and sequencing across the broader product surface. Education is central to CrossFit's identity and has significant room to grow. The foundation is an older, layered stack of in-house software and vendor tools.

This role requires someone resilient and responsive, strong at strategy, and disciplined about tight feedback loops: a person who can bring structure and clarity to ambiguity, make disciplined trade-offs, and deliver measurable results.

Responsibilities

  • Product Strategy & Roadmap:
    • Define and own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for Education, in alignment with company priorities and business objectives.
    • Establish clear product goals, success metrics, and KPIs, and regularly evaluate performance against expected outcomes.
    • Use customer insights, product analytics, market trends, and business data to identify opportunities and guide product decisions.
    • Balance learner experience, business impact, technical investment, and available resources, and make and communicate clear trade-off decisions when priorities compete.
    • Bring an informed point of view on where online learning is heading, then commit fully to the direction the business chooses.
  • Product Execution:
    • Lead the product lifecycle from discovery and validation through development, launch, adoption, measurement, and iteration.
    • Guide product decisions for Education's learner experience, course registration, content authoring and delivery, learning platforms, and credentialing, including integrations across existing systems.
    • Evaluate build, buy, modernize, or replace options for legacy platforms and vendor tools, considering user needs, technical dependencies, migration costs, and long-term value.
    • Ensure requirements clearly define the customer problem, business need, expected outcome, and measures of success.
    • Partner with Engineering and Design to scope initiatives and sequence work across quick wins, foundational fixes, and new capabilities.
    • Support launches with go-to-market, communication, training, and adoption plans in partnership with business stakeholders.
    • Contribute to foundational platform capabilities that cut across products, such as data privacy and consent, localization, and marketing enablement.
  • Customer & Business Impact:
    • Partner with Education leaders and program owners to identify learner and instructor pain points, distinguish underlying problems from proposed solutions, and prioritize improvements across the learner journey.
    • Establish and improve instrumentation for enrollment, course completion, conversion, learner retention, and revenue per learner, including where existing data is incomplete.
    • Run experiments across acquisition, activation, upgrades, and re-engagement, using results to refine product and growth priorities.
    • Build tight feedback loops through research, analytics, and direct engagement with learners, instructors, and staff, and turn what you learn into decisions quickly.
    • Tie product investments to measurable customer and business outcomes rather than feature delivery alone.
  • Collaboration & Influence:
    • Serve as the key Product partner to Education leadership, and communicate strategy, roadmap decisions, progress, risks, and results to executives and other stakeholders.
    • Establish operating rhythms that create visibility into roadmap progress, dependencies, risks, and decisions.
    • Identify and resolve barriers to execution across teams and functions.
    • Model strong product practices, including discovery, prioritization, and measurement, and share them with peers.
    • Coordinate with product owners for adjacent products to align strategy and sequencing.

Knowledge and Skills

  • Strong product judgment, with the ability to connect customer needs, business strategy, technology, and financial outcomes.
  • Knowledge of education technology, including learning management systems, content authoring, course delivery, credentialing, and learner-facing experiences, and/or deep experience in growth: funnel analysis, experimentation, activation, conversion, and retention. Depth in both is ideal.
  • Ability to define meaningful funnel and learning metrics, improve measurement capabilities, and use experimentation to inform product decisions.
  • Experience navigating legacy systems, vendor integrations, and fragmented data environments, with sound judgment on technical and migration trade-offs.
  • Strong strategic thinking, paired with resilience and responsiveness. You turn feedback into decisions quickly and stay steady when plans change.
  • Ability to prioritize investments and make difficult trade-offs in a resource-constrained environment.
  • Skill at finding the real problem behind a stated request, and at saying no in a way that keeps the relationship intact.
  • Strong understanding of modern software development and experience partnering closely with Engineering and Design.
  • Uses modern AI tools (e.g., Claude) fluently to accelerate discovery, requirements, analysis, and delivery.
  • Experience with lifecycle marketing and personalization tooling preferred.
  • Excellent communication and executive presentation skills, with demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and create alignment across functions.
  • Comfortable operating in an evolving environment, bringing structure and clarity to ambiguity.
  • Strong ownership, accountability, and bias toward execution.
  • Understanding of the CrossFit ecosystem, Affiliate model, or fitness industry preferred.

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • 7+ years of product management experience for Senior, or 10+ years for Principal, including significant ownership of digital products or platforms.
  • Experience with education technology, certification or credentialing, online learning, or learner growth products, and/or growth product experience across acquisition, activation, conversion, and retention.
  • Familiarity with learning standards (such as SCORM or xAPI), international localization, registration and payment flows, or membership-based education models preferred.
  • Demonstrated success launching and improving products that delivered measurable customer and business outcomes, ideally in an older or complex technology environment.
  • Experience partnering closely with Engineering, Design, and senior business leaders.
  • Experience with consumer, B2B, marketplace, membership, subscription, fitness, or community-based digital products preferred.

Compensation

Additional Information
